title: Quant Perf Dashboard Spec (FP8/INT8) — Models x GPUs x Runtime Version
author: Allison Grant
content:
## Purpose
This page specifies the **Quant Perf** dashboard(s) used to monitor FP8/INT8 inference performance across Redwood’s hosted “top models”, primary GPU SKUs, and runtime versions.

Primary users:
- Runtime kernels + scheduling teams (triage + optimization attribution)
- SRE / Observability (perf lab stability, regression alerts)
- Release Engineering (gating + “go/no-go” on runtime trains)

The dashboard is designed to answer:
1) **Did FP8/INT8 regress** (end-to-end and kernel-level), and where?
2) Is the regression **model-specific**, **GPU-specific**, **runtime-version-specific**, or **scheduler-policy-specific**?
3) Do we see behavior consistent with **kernel auto-selection changes**, **KV-cache interaction**, or **queueing/batching policy** changes?

---

## Data sources and scope
### Sources
The dashboard consumes metrics emitted by:
- **Benchmark Lab harness** (nightly/adhoc runs): end-to-end TTFT/TPOT, throughput, per-phase timing, metadata (model/GPU/runtime pins).
- **Serving runtime perf logs** (structured JSON events): phase breakdown, selected kernel IDs, shapes, GPU clocks (when present).
- **Scheduler instrumentation**: queue wait time histograms split by quant mode + phase.
- **Perf-canary**: comparator outputs (baseline vs candidate; robust stats; pass/fail state).

### Environments
- Primary: **perf-lab** (dedicated nodes, controlled clocks where supported)
- Secondary: **staging** canary cohort (only for “real traffic shape” confirmation; not used for strict gating)

### Granularity expectations
- End-to-end metrics: per scenario run, aggregated by model x GPU x quant_mode x runtime_version
- Kernel metrics: sampled distributions by op/kind (GEMM, attention) + selected kernel family

---

## Tagging / dimensions (REQUIRED)
The dashboard relies on consistent tags. All benchmark and canary metrics MUST include the following dimensions.

### Required tags
- `model_id` (e.g., `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`, `qwen2.5-72b-instruct`, `mistral-large-instruct`)
- `model_family` (e.g., `llama`, `qwen`, `mistral`)
- `route_type` (one of: `chat`, `completions`, `embeddings`, `rerank`) — for this sprint mostly `chat`/`completions`
- `scenario` (see scenarios below; stable identifier)
- `quant_mode` (one of: `fp16`, `fp8`, `int8`) — **fp16 acts as control**
- `gpu_sku` (e.g., `a100-80gb`, `h100-sxm`, `h200-sxm`, `l40s`)
- `gpu_count` (string integer, e.g., `1`, `2`, `8`)
- `runtime_version` (human label, e.g., `runtime-2025.10.1`) and `runtime_commit` (git SHA)
- `container_digest` (immutable image reference)
- `region` (e.g., `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`) OR `perf_lab_cluster` (if region isn’t meaningful)
- `phase` (one of: `prefill`, `decode`, `e2e`) for phase-split panels

### Strongly recommended tags
- `kernel_family` (e.g., `cutlass`, `cublaslt`, `flashattn`, `custom_fp8_attn_v2`)
- `kernel_id` (stable identifier emitted by runtime; used for distribution panels)
- `shape_bucket` (string bucket like `m=..._n=..._k=...` or `seq=...` for attention)
- `scheduler_policy` (e.g., `baseline`, `quant_decode_batchcap_v1`)
- `streaming` (`true`/`false`)

### Notes
- If a metric is missing `runtime_commit` or `container_digest`, it is treated as **non-reproducible** and excluded from gating views.
- `scenario` names must be stable across time; scenario parameters go in metadata logs and run artifacts.

---

## Scenario catalog (for grouping and filters)
The dashboard supports these canonical scenarios (minimum set):

1) `chat_streaming_mixed_v1`
- Streaming chat; mixed prompt lengths; concurrency sweep.
- Primary metrics: **TTFT**, **TPOT**, p95 tail.

2) `chat_nonstreaming_decodeheavy_v1`
- Non-streaming; short prompts; long decode.
- Primary metric: **tokens/sec** and TPOT stability.

3) `completions_prefillheavy_longctx_v1`
- Long context prefill focus (regression hotspot for FP8).
- Primary metric: **prefill latency**, TTFT.

4) `microbench_gemm_v1` and `microbench_attn_v1`
- Kernel-level microbenchmarks for attribution.
- Primary metric: **op latency** and kernel selection distribution.

---

## Dashboard layout and panels
This spec assumes Grafana-style dashboards, but panel definitions are tool-agnostic.

### A. “Executive” row (fast regression read)
1) **Quant Perf Canary Status (pass/fail)**
- Single-stat per (gpu_sku, quant_mode) for last nightly run.
- Shows: `PASS`, `WARN`, `FAIL`, `NO_DATA`.
- Links: comparator artifact / run ID.

2) **Top regressions table (last 24–72h)**
- Table sorted by worst delta vs baseline.
- Columns:
  - model_id, scenario, gpu_sku, quant_mode
  - metric_name (TTFT_p95 / TPOT_p95 / tokens_per_sec)
  - baseline value, candidate value, delta %, z-score (if available)
  - runtime_version, runtime_commit

3) **Coverage / freshness**
- Heatmap: model_id x gpu_sku with last successful timestamp.
- Purpose: detect silent gaps due to lab contention / failed runs.


### B. End-to-end latency and throughput
4) **TTFT (p50/p95/p99) — streaming scenarios**
- Timeseries + last-value table.
- Filters: scenario contains `streaming`, quant_mode, gpu_sku, model_family.
- Split by: quant_mode.

5) **TPOT (p50/p95/p99) — streaming scenarios**
- Same structure as TTFT; focus on **tail** (p95/p99).

6) **Throughput — tokens/sec (decode) and requests/min**
- Two y-axes or separate panels.
- Notes: throughput must be compared only when concurrency is consistent; panel includes a concurrency filter.

7) **Prefill vs decode breakdown**
- Stacked bar (or two-panel pair): `prefill_ms` and `decode_ms` per request.
- Goal: quickly identify “prefill-only” FP8 regressions.

8) **Cost proxy (ms/token) and normalized efficiency**
- Panel A: `ms_per_output_token` (lower is better)
- Panel B: `tokens_per_second_per_gpu` (higher is better)
- Used for triage; not primary gating unless explicitly noted.


### C. Scheduler and queueing health (tail latency drivers)
9) **Scheduler queue wait time (prefill vs decode)**
- Histogram quantiles (p50/p95/p99) split by `phase` and `quant_mode`.
- Purpose: detect regressions caused by batching caps, interleaving policy, or lab contention.

10) **Batch size distribution (decode)**
- Histogram: observed decode batch sizes.
- Split by: quant_mode and scheduler_policy.
- Expectation: quant batch-cap overrides will shift distribution left; tail may improve.

11) **Concurrency vs TPOT p95**
- XY plot: concurrency on X, TPOT p95 on Y.
- Repeat per gpu_sku and quant_mode.
- Purpose: highlight nonlinear queueing thresholds.


### D. Kernel attribution (why did performance change?)
12) **Kernel selection distribution (top-k kernels)**
- Bar chart by `kernel_id` with % share.
- Filters: op kind (GEMM / attention), model_family, gpu_sku, quant_mode, scenario.
- Expectation: auto-selector changes should be visible immediately.

13) **Kernel latency by shape bucket**
- Heatmap: shape_bucket vs latency (median, p95).
- Used to locate “one bad shape” driving end-to-end regressions.

14) **FP8/INT8 fallback rate**
- Timeseries: % of requests where quant path fell back to FP16 (or non-quant kernel) due to unsupported op/shape.
- Any increase should be investigated; fallback can look like perf regression.


### E. Correctness / guardrails (quick check)
15) **Numeric drift check status**
- Single-stat + table for last runs.
- Columns: model_id, quant_mode, drift_metric (e.g., `logits_l2`, `topk_agreement`), threshold, status.
- Note: This is not a full quality eval; it is a guardrail to prevent obvious breakage.

16) **Error rate during benchmarks**
- Panel: request error %, timeout %, OOM count.
- Must be visible next to perf metrics to avoid misattribution.

---

## Dashboard variables (filters)
Required dashboard-level variables:
- `model_family`
- `model_id`
- `scenario`
- `quant_mode`
- `gpu_sku`
- `runtime_version` and `runtime_commit`
- `scheduler_policy`
- `region` / `perf_lab_cluster`
- `streaming`

Defaults:
- `quant_mode`: show `fp8` and `int8` and `fp16` (control)
- `scenario`: default to `chat_streaming_mixed_v1`
- `gpu_sku`: default to `h100-sxm` (if available) + allow multi-select

---

## Alerting spec (regression detection)
Alerts are intended for **nightly canary** results and for obvious breakages in metric emission.

### Alert routing
- Primary Slack: `#eng-runtime`
- Secondary Slack: `#eng-sre` (only for lab stability / no-data)
- On-call / paging: **not enabled** by default (internal perf canary); enable only after 30 days of stable signal.

### Alert categories
#### 1) Performance regression (FAIL)
Triggers when all conditions hold:
- Comparator has a valid baseline and candidate (N>=5 runs recommended; use robust aggregation)
- Scenario is in the “gating set” (see below)
- Regression exceeds threshold and is not allowlisted

**Default FAIL thresholds (end-to-end):**
- TTFT p95: **+10%** or worse vs baseline
- TPOT p95: **+8%** or worse vs baseline
- Tokens/sec (decode): **-7%** or worse vs baseline

**Default FAIL thresholds (microbench):**
- Attention kernel median latency: **+8%**
- GEMM kernel median latency: **+6%**

Additional rule:
- If TTFT p95 regresses **>15%**, mark as **FAIL even if throughput improves** (TTFT is customer-visible for streaming).

#### 2) Performance regression (WARN)
- TTFT p95: +5% to +10%
- TPOT p95: +4% to +8%
- Tokens/sec: -4% to -7%

WARN notifies `#eng-runtime` but does not block release by itself; it requires an owner to annotate root cause or add an allowlist entry with expiry.

#### 3) No data / coverage regression
- No successful run for a required (model_family, gpu_sku, quant_mode, gating scenario) combination in > 36h.
- Alerts `#eng-sre` and `#eng-runtime` with the missing matrix cell(s).

#### 4) Correctness guardrail failure
- Any drift check marked FAIL for fp8/int8 vs fp16 on gating prompt set.
- Always notify `#eng-runtime`; also notify Release Engineering (`#eng-releases`) when candidate is part of a release train.


### Gating set (initial)
The dashboard defines the “gating set” for alerts as:
- Scenarios: `chat_streaming_mixed_v1`, `completions_prefillheavy_longctx_v1`
- GPU SKUs: `h100-sxm`, `a100-80gb` (expand to `h200-sxm` and `l40s` as lab capacity stabilizes)
- Quant modes: `fp8`, `int8`
- Model families: `llama`, `qwen`, `mistral` (one representative model_id per family in gating; full matrix runs remain visible but non-gating)


### Allowlisting policy
Allowlisting is permitted only when:
- Root cause is understood and documented (link PR/issue)
- Allowlist has an **expiry date** (<= 14 days default)
- A mitigation exists (e.g., pin kernel family, disable for gpu_sku, or rollback)

Allowlist dimensions must be precise (e.g., `(model_id, gpu_sku, quant_mode, scenario)`), not global.

---

## Metric naming conventions (implementation guidance)
This section is guidance for implementers to ensure consistent querying.

### Recommended metric names
End-to-end (benchmark harness):
- `bench_ttft_ms{...}`
- `bench_tpot_ms{...}`
- `bench_tokens_per_sec{...}`
- `bench_prefill_ms{...}`, `bench_decode_ms{...}`
- `bench_error_rate{...}`

Scheduler (runtime):
- `sched_queue_wait_ms_bucket{phase=...,quant_mode=...,...}` (histogram)
- `sched_decode_batch_size_bucket{quant_mode=...,...}`

Kernel attribution (runtime spans/logs → metrics):
- `kernel_selected_total{kernel_id=...,kernel_family=...,op=...,quant_mode=...,...}`
- `kernel_op_latency_ms_bucket{op=...,kernel_id=...,shape_bucket=...,...}`

Correctness:
- `quant_drift_metric{metric=...,quant_mode=...,...}` plus `quant_drift_status{status=PASS|FAIL,...}`

### Required “identity” fields
Every emitted timeseries must include: `runtime_commit`, `container_digest`, `run_id`.

---

## Operational notes
- The dashboard must support **annotations** for runtime releases (e.g., `runtime-2025.10.1`) and large kernel/scheduler changes. Release Engineering owns annotation hygiene.
- For any panel showing deltas, the baseline selection must be explicit (pinned by `runtime_commit` or “last green” canary).
- Panels intended for triage should deep-link to:
  - benchmark artifact (run_id)
  - tracing view (selected requests)
  - kernel-selection logs (if enabled)

---

## Ownership and change management
Owner team: **Eng Platform → Observability (Dashboards & Alerts)**
- Primary owner: Allison Grant
- Backup: Aisha Bello

Change process:
1) Proposed changes via PR in observability pack (dashboard JSON) and update this spec.
2) Review required from: Runtime Perf (Noah Patel or delegate) and SRE Perf Lab (Sean Gallagher or delegate).
3) Changes that affect alert thresholds require sign-off from Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien).

---

## Appendix: Quick validation checklist (before enabling alerts)
- [ ] All gating scenarios emit TTFT/TPOT/tokens_sec with required tags.
- [ ] Comparator job produces baseline/candidate with the same scenario parameters.
- [ ] Dashboard filters work with multi-select on model_id and gpu_sku.
- [ ] “No data” alert is quiet under normal lab load (no false positives).
- [ ] At least one intentional regression test triggers WARN/FAIL as expected.

(End of page)
